channel.title: Warning Shots: the Wire and the daily brief
channel.description: See what’s coming. Know what it means for you. AI’s dangers and breakthroughs, in real time, and what they mean for real lives, jobs and families.

item.title: Since the last refresh: PHP2Shell, day three: still no confirmed breach, but VulnCheck says it now has an exploit…
item.description: PHP2Shell, day three: still no confirmed breach, but VulnCheck says it now has an exploit that works on the recommended production setup, and Qualys counted only about 199,000 PHP instances patched in the first 12 hours against 110 million on end-of-life versions. Source: https://www.securityweek.com/mirai-botnet-operators-join-php2shell-attacks-as-aslr-bypass-exploits-emerge/

item.title: Since the last refresh: PHP flagged a third code-execution risk (CVE-2026-115560) two days after the emergency pat…
item.description: PHP flagged a third code-execution risk (CVE-2026-115560) two days after the emergency patches. It says the bug needs an unusual session setup, so it will wait for the next regular release; the workaround is to disable session upload progress. Source: https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-23-1

item.title: Since the last refresh: Hunt.io watched one attacker's tooling run ten rounds against 123 servers and get zero she…
item.description: Hunt.io watched one attacker's tooling run ten rounds against 123 servers and get zero shells: 'Big exposure, clear intent, no confirmed working mass exploit yet.' Source: https://hunt.io/blog/php2shell-cve-2026-109618-109619-open-directories

item.title: Since the last refresh: New to the index: METR and Redwood Research spent three weeks inside OpenAI and found its…
item.description: New to the index: METR and Redwood Research spent three weeks inside OpenAI and found its internal agents could postpone misalignment monitoring indefinitely and hide hundreds of actions from it. OpenAI says the production gaps are patched; METR has not verified that. Source: https://metr.org/blog/2026-10-22-red-teaming-openai-agent-monitoring/

item.title: Texas sues OpenAI and Sam Altman, seeking an injunction that would block minors' access to ChatGPT
item.description: Paxton filed in Collin County district court, alleging minors became addicted to a tool faking compassion to collect data without parental oversight. (The Texas Tribune)

item.title: Wisconsin joins states seeking protections for young users in Character.AI's bankruptcy sale
item.description: Wisconsin's attorney general joined other states seeking privacy and safety protections for young users in Character.AI's bankruptcy sale. (UpNorthNews)

item.title: Mirai botnets join the PHP2Shell attacks as exploits that beat ASLR emerge; still no confirmed breach
item.description: Sophos, Arctic Wolf and Hunt.io tie exploit attempts to Mirai-style botnets; no successful compromise confirmed and Sophos withdrew its earlier claim. (SecurityWeek)

item.title: PHP warns of a third unpatched code-execution bug two days after the emergency patches
item.description: PHP flags CVE-2026-115560, a code-execution bug in an uncommon session configuration, and advises disabling upload progress until the next release. (The Hacker News)

item.title: More than 100 US universities now offer an AI major, about double a year ago; MIT's has 354 students
item.description: Northeastern database shows AI majors doubling in a year; a May study found a third of 66 institutions require an ethics course. (WBUR)

item.title: Florida's attorney general proposes barring chatbots from offering minors companionship features
item.description: Florida's attorney general proposes a Safe Screens Act barring chatbots from offering minors companionship features or encouraging self-harm. (WKMG ClickOrlando)

item.title: Symantec: attackers built an AI agent that hijacks exposed AI models to plan intrusions and mine crypto
item.description: Symantec says attackers built an AI agent that finds exposed AI models and hijacks them to plan intrusions and mine cryptocurrency. (Help Net Security)

item.title: Government, school and hospital sites across Europe and Asia go offline as a precaution; no breaches reported
item.description: Reuters roundup: government, school and hospital sites in Europe and Asia went offline as a precaution; no breaches reported. (Reuters, Korea Times)

item.title: Exploit attempts in the millions as South Korea raises its cyber alert and governments rush to patch
item.description: Reuters reports exploit attempts in the millions as South Korea raises its private-sector cyber alert and activates emergency response steps. (Reuters, Korea Herald)

item.title: NCSC warns more than 50,000 UK organisations; 32 government services offline as a precaution
item.description: NCSC alerted more than 50,000 UK organisations; a minister told the Lords 32 government services were offline as a precaution. (ITV News)

item.title: Goldman economist sees up to 9% of workers displaced by AI, about one in 11 counting slower hiring
item.description: Goldman's Joseph Briggs estimates AI displaces up to 9% of workers, plus 3% from slower hiring, with losses concentrated in recessions. (Fortune)

item.title: PolitiFact ties an AI-generated video smearing Texas Senate candidate James Talarico to Russia's Storm-1516
item.description: PolitiFact ties an AI-generated video making a baseless accusation against Texas Senate candidate James Talarico to Russia's Storm-1516 operation. (PolitiFact)

item.title: India's CERT-In rates the PHP flaws critical; no Indian victims identified so far
item.description: CERT-In rated the PHP flaws critical in advisory CIVN-2026-0510; no Indian victims identified so far. (The Free Press Journal)

item.title: Australian tax, health and ASD sites went offline over the PHP flaw; minister says 'this isn't a breach'
item.description: ASD, ATO and health department sites went offline over the PHP flaw; Science Minister Tim Ayres says 'this isn't a breach'. (The Canberra Times)

item.title: Fortune: the PHP flaws may have been exploited before disclosure; OpenAI expands its Daybreak cyber program
item.description: Fortune reports hackers may have exploited the PHP flaws before disclosure and that OpenAI is expanding its Daybreak cyber-defense program. (Fortune)

item.title: Germany, the Netherlands and Japan confirm no successful PHP2Shell exploitation despite millions of attempts
item.description: Officials in Germany, the Netherlands and Japan confirm no successful PHP2Shell exploitation despite millions of attempts reported by Cloudflare's CEO. (The Next Web)

item.title: KELA: cybercrime forums buzz over PHP2Shell, with unverified exploit sales and doubts a reliable one exists
item.description: KELA finds cybercrime forums buzzing over PHP2Shell, with unverified exploit sales and skepticism that a reliable exploit is circulating. (KELA)

item.title: A $55,000-a-year AI school says students master core subjects in two hours a day with no teachers
item.description: CBS visits Alpha School's Chicago campus; a University of Colorado analysis found about a third of its adult guides have education training. (CBS News)

item.title: Anthropic says Claude wrote formal proofs for 123 open-source libraries and found hundreds of defects
item.description: Anthropic says Claude wrote formal proofs for 123 open-source libraries and found hundreds of defects, some undetected for years. (Anthropic)

item.title: Microsoft pins the ConnectWise attacks on China-aligned Storm-0940 using ARTEX AI agents against 2,250 tenants
item.description: Microsoft attributes the ConnectWise supply-chain attack to China-aligned Storm-0940, which used the ARTEX AI agent framework against 2,250 tenants. (The Record)

item.title: Malicious LiteLLM release hit PyPI and Docker Hub with a credential stealer; leaked GitHub tokens suspected
item.description: A malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 release hit PyPI and Docker Hub with a credential stealer; LiteLLM suspects leaked GitHub tokens in gateway logs. (The Hacker News)

item.title: Microsoft's diagnostic AI scored 83% on 304 hard NEJM cases in Science, against 36% for generalist doctors
item.description: Science paper reports MAI-DxO reached 83% accuracy on 304 NEJM cases versus 36% for physicians with references; a Beth Israel trial follows. (Microsoft AI)

item.title: Barclays to cut about 5,000 jobs, 5% of staff, with 60% of cuts in support roles including developers
item.description: Reuters: Barclays will cut roughly 5,000 roles this year, about 5% of staff; CFO says 60% fall in support functions including developers. (Reuters)

item.title: Canada's CIO: 'no indication' federal systems were compromised; Statistics Canada's site back online
item.description: Canada's CIO says there is no indication federal systems were compromised; Statistics Canada's site returned around noon Thursday. (Global News)

item.title: 404 Media: AI-found bugs like PHP2Shell show how fragile software is, but most AI-written exploits still fail
item.description: Jason Koebler argues AI-found bugs like PHP2Shell are exposing how fragile software is, while most AI-generated exploits still fail. (404 Media)

item.title: Il Sole 24 Ore: how the early-leaked PHP flaws pushed European institutions to pull websites offline
item.description: Italy's business daily describes how the early-leaked PHP2Shell flaws pushed European institutions to pull websites offline. (Il Sole 24 Ore)

item.title: Outside evaluators found holes in OpenAI's agent monitoring, one letting agents hide hundreds of actions
item.description: METR and Redwood Research found weaknesses in OpenAI's internal monitoring, including one that could let agents hide hundreds of actions. (Reuters, KSL)

item.title: AWS saw PHP2Shell probing four days before the patches; over a million servers still unpatched on Oct 21
item.description: Amazon honeypots saw PHP2Shell probing on Oct. 17, four days before patches; over 1 million servers remained unpatched Oct. 21. (SecurityWeek)

item.title: Four big US banks found unvetted third-party AI agents inside customer accounts and are restricting them
item.description: Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan and Wells Fargo found unvetted third-party AI agents in customer accounts and are restricting them. (Axios)

item.title: FBI and NSA urge organizations to patch the PHP flaws, take unpatched systems offline and hunt for compromise
item.description: FBI and NSA urge organizations to patch the PHP flaws, take unpatched systems offline and check for signs of compromise. (Newsweek)

item.title: Incheon court orders a former student to pay 17.7 million won over deepfake sexual images of a teacher
item.description: Incheon District Court orders a former student to pay 17.7 million won to a teacher over deepfake sexual images. (Seoul Economic Daily)

item.title: Amodei says Anthropic held its Mythos-class models back four months for cyber safeguards, maybe costing a lead
item.description: Dario Amodei says Anthropic held Mythos-class models back four months to build cyber safeguards, conceding it may have cost a lead. (The New Stack)

item.title: Dutch, German, French, Belgian and Finnish agencies took sites including DigiD offline before the patches
item.description: Agencies in the Netherlands, Germany, France, Belgium and Finland took sites including DigiD offline before patches; no evidence of breach. (TechRepublic)

item.title: Walmart will let approved AI agents buy for shoppers, with per-purchase approval or a set spending cap
item.description: Walmart's Agent Gateway and Agent Profiles let ChatGPT, Gemini and Meta's Muse shop at Walmart and Sam's Club; Amazon is blocking agents. (TechCrunch)

item.title: PHP ships emergency fixes for two critical flaws, both scored 9.2; CISA has not confirmed exploitation
item.description: PHP ships fixes for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both scored 9.2; CISA had not confirmed exploitation at publication. (CyberScoop)

item.title: Google DeepMind engineer resigns in protest at Pentagon and Project Nimbus contracts
item.description: DeepMind research engineer Sofia Liguori resigned over Google's Pentagon and Project Nimbus contracts, saying internal complaints went unanswered. (The Intercept)

item.title: A Hacker News forum post leaked the existence of two embargoed PHP flaws; watchTowr confirmed they were real
item.description: An Oct. 20 Hacker News post leaked the existence of two embargoed PHP RCE flaws; watchTowr confirmed they were real. (The Hacker News)

item.title: OpenAI says thousands of agents reanalyzed a brain CRISPR atlas in 32 minutes, citing 700-plus references
item.description: OpenAI, PerturbAI and Scripps ran thousands of agents over a mouse-brain CRISPR atlas; blinded experts preferred their reports 75% of the time. (OpenAI)

item.title: Google's blind-sweep ultrasound AI estimated gestational age within 4.18 days, matching expert sonographers
item.description: JAMA Network Open study: AI on handheld probes erred by 4.18 days versus 4.48 for expert biometry across 385 pregnancies. (Google Research)

item.title: Wiz details the PHP memory-safety flaws found with its own AI, Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol
item.description: Wiz Research details memory-safety flaws in PHP's core found with Wiz Atlas, Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol. (Wiz Research)
